value.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for independent second opinions from a panel of stated perspectives
value.lets_workers: Get second opinions before a decision: define a panel of independent reviewers, each with a stated perspective and, where possible, a model family different from the producer's; have each give a take alone from the same sealed packet, with no reviewer seeing another's; check that independence before anyone reads the views; write a synthesis that leads with where the reviewers disagree and where each disagreement goes next; have someone else audit it; and leave the decision to a person.
value.not_for: Choosing between finished options by taste, which the taste palettes pack does, or measuring which option is better, which the evaluation design pack does. A panel routes such disagreements to them.

flow.when: The plan or draft, the decision it informs and who produced it.
Each reviewer alone, as a separate attempt.
The sealed views, read in the fixed order.
Someone who wrote none of it checks the quotes and routes.
A person decides, or decides later.
A factual disagreement gets an evaluation.
A disagreement of taste becomes a palette.

value.worked_example: Made-up: a literacy program's plan, drafted by a model run, to replace paper sign-in sheets with tablet check-in. Three reviewers on three families, one shared with the producer and labeled, take it alone. Their sealed views disagree on a fact, whether check-ins survive a site's evening wifi outages, and on a value, whether quicker check-in is worth a screen some learners cannot read. The program director proceeds with changes and leaves the factual question to a week-long test.

value.title: How a panel gives independent takes and a person decides
value.category_reason: A reusable procedure with guardrails, followed by every verb in this pack.
lifecycle: define-panel records the producer and its model family, picks three to five perspective cards, gives each reviewer a family, and fixes the shared packet, the deadline and the reading seed.
give-view runs once per reviewer as a separate attempt, each sealed on submission.
check-independence confirms every view used the packet, was sealed in time and names no other reviewer, before anyone reads them.
synthesize-disagreements reads the views in the fixed order and leads with where they disagree.
audit-synthesis, by someone who wrote none of it, rechecks every quote and route.
decide is a person's: proceed, proceed with changes, do not proceed or decide later.
rules: Independence is the point: a view written after reading another is a second copy, not a second opinion.
Disagreements are the output; agreement among reviewers who share blind spots is weak evidence.
A factual disagreement is settled by evidence, a value disagreement by the person, a taste disagreement by a palette and a scope disagreement by asking the requester.
Each reviewer spends only its worker's own allowance; this pack grants no spending.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; they never enqueue.

value.title: Who sits on a panel
value.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same request and allowance give the same panel shape.
rules: Three to five reviewers, each with a different perspective card; at least one looks for how the plan fails and one stands for the people it serves.
A perspective is a role, never a real person and never an imitation of one.
The producer, whether a person or a model run, is not on its own panel, and neither is the synthesizer.
Record the producer's model family and each reviewer's. Prefer families other than the producer's, and more than one across the panel; a reviewer on the producer's family needs a stated reason.
Reviewer ids are opaque, such as r1 and r2, so an id says nothing about a perspective or a family.
Each reviewer is a separate attempt with its own lease and an execution report naming the exact provider and model.

value.title: Keeping the takes independent
value.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same views and seed give the same check and order.
rules: Every reviewer gets the same packet: the artifact by digest, the question and the instructions; only the perspective card differs.
The packet leaves out the producer's view of its own work and every other reviewer's take.
Reviewers share no conversation, memory, cache or scratch space.
A view is sealed by the SHA-256 of its canonical JSON when submitted, and nobody reads any view until all are sealed or the deadline passes.
A late view is kept and marked late. A view that names or quotes another reviewer is excluded and redone, because its independence is lost.
Views are read in ascending order of the SHA-256 of the seed, a colon and the reviewer id, so their order does not depend on who finished first.

value.title: Synthesizing where reviewers disagree
value.category_reason: A zero-call deterministic procedure: the same views give the same structure.
rules: Lead with disagreements. Quote every side exactly from the sealed views, with the reviewer id and perspective.
Name each disagreement's kind and route, and say what would resolve it.
Keep agreements to a short list, and list every point only one reviewer raised.
Never settle a disagreement by counting reviewers; a count is information only, with the panel size.
Say plainly when there is no disagreement, and why it may be real or correlated.
The synthesis recommends nothing; a person decides.

kinds.taste: It turns on preference between versions: route to a taste palette.
